units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
But I want to see her. I want her to come here.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Never!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: She came here once as your guest. She must come now as mine . That is but fair.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: She should never have come here.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Rising .
It is too late, Arthur, to say that now.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Moves away .
Rising .
Margaret, if you knew where Mrs. Erlynne went last night, after she left this house, you would not sit in the same room with her. It was absolutely shameless, the whole thing.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Arthur, I can’t bear it any longer. I must tell you. Last night—
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Enter PARKER with a tray on which lie LADY WINDERMERE’S fan and a card .
Mrs. Erlynne has called to return your ladyship’s fan which she took away by mistake last night. Mrs. Erlynne has written a message on the card.
units.name: PARKER

units.text: Oh, ask Mrs. Erlynne to be kind enough to come up.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Reads card .
Say I shall be very glad to see her.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Exit PARKER.
She wants to see me, Arthur.
Takes card and looks at it .
Margaret, I beg you not to. Let me see her first, at any rate. She’s a very dangerous woman. She is the most dangerous woman I know. You don’t realise what you’re doing.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: It is right that I should see her.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: My child, you may be on the brink of a great sorrow. Don’t go to meet it. It is absolutely necessary that I should see her before you do.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Why should it be necessary?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Enter PARKER.
Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: PARKER

units.text: Enter MRS. ERLYNNE.
Exit PARKER.
How do you do, Lady Windermere?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: To LORD WINDERMERE.

How do you do? Do you know, Lady Windermere, I am so sorry about your fan. I can’t imagine how I made such a silly mistake. Most stupid of me. And as I was driving in your direction, I thought I would take the opportunity of returning your property in person with many apologies for my carelessness, and of bidding you good-bye.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Good-bye?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Moves towards sofa with MRS. ERLYNNE and sits down beside her .
Are you going away, then, Mrs. Erlynne?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Yes; I am going to live abroad again. The English climate doesn’t suit me. My—heart is affected here, and that I don’t like. I prefer living in the south. London is too full of fogs and—and serious people, Lord Windermere. Whether the fogs produce the serious people or whether the serious people produce the fogs, I don’t know, but the whole thing rather gets on my nerves, and so I’m leaving this afternoon by the Club Train.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: This afternoon? But I wanted so much to come and see you.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: How kind of you! But I am afraid I have to go.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Shall I never see you again, Mrs. Erlynne?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: I am afraid not. Our lives lie too far apart. But there is a little thing I would like you to do for me. I want a photograph of you, Lady Windermere—would you give me one? You don’t know how gratified I should be.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Oh, with pleasure. There is one on that table. I’ll show it to you.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Goes across to the table .
Coming up to MRS. ERLYNNE and speaking in a low voice .
It is monstrous your intruding yourself here after your conduct last night.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: With an amused smile .
My dear Windermere, manners before morals!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Returning .
I’m afraid it is very flattering—I am not so pretty as that.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE
